item.title: [Strong Feedback] Auto-run still requires manual confirmation and breaks SOLO/Agent workflows
item.body:
I have already enabled “Auto-run” in Trae / SOLO, but in actual use, Trae still frequently asks me to manually click “Run”.

This is not an occasional issue. It has existed for a long time and seriously affects the Agent long-task experience.

My feedback is simple:

1. If the product provides an “Auto-run” mode, it should clearly explain which commands will actually run automatically and which commands will still be blocked.
2. If commands such as rm, rm -rf, Remove-Item, Copy-Item, or cross-workspace file operations are always forced to require confirmation, then the mode should not simply be called “Auto-run”, because that is misleading.
3. The current behavior is very frustrating: users believe auto-run has been configured correctly, but the Agent stops halfway and waits for a manual confirmation. Several hours later, the user finds that the task never continued.
4. For SOLO / Agent workflows, this is not a minor UX problem. It breaks the core automation experience. Long-running tasks, automated testing, automated builds, cleanup of temporary files, and file copying can all be interrupted by one confirmation dialog.
5. I understand the need for safety, but the current design is too coarse-grained and not transparent enough.

I suggest adding a more advanced and configurable permission model:

- Allow users to define trusted workspaces.
- Allow users to configure command allowlists and blocklists.
- Do not rely only on simple keyword matching. The full command should be parsed and evaluated.
- For destructive commands, allow safer scoped rules, such as “only allow deletion inside the current project’s temporary directory”.
- Support “trust for this session”.
- Support “always trust this project”.
- Clearly mark commands that will still be blocked even when Auto-run is enabled.

The most frustrating part is not the safety restriction itself. The real problem is that the behavior is not transparent, not predictable, and not consistent.

If the Trae team actually uses SOLO for real project work, this should be very easy to reproduce: the Agent modifies code, runs tests, cleans temporary files, copies build artifacts, and then suddenly gets stuck waiting for a manual confirmation. This creates a very broken workflow.

Please do not end this issue with another generic “for safety reasons” answer. Safety is important, but advanced users also need a controllable, explainable, and configurable automation permission model.

Right now, the product looks like an Agent, but in practice it behaves like a semi-automatic script that still requires the user to sit there and click buttons. This conflicts with the positioning of SOLO.
